components.name: Application
components.role: application traffic source inside a container, one of several stacked instances

components.name: TCP/IP
components.role: socket buffering and transport-protocol processing layer

components.name: Container Virtual Switch (bridge)
components.role: virtual bridge connecting containers to the host network stack

components.name: Qdiscs
components.role: hierarchical packet schedulers that operate in parallel across CPU cores

components.name: TX Rings
components.role: per-queue descriptor rings buffering packets before NIC transmission

components.name: Network Interface
components.role: NIC-side stage performing scheduling and hardware offloads

components.name: NIC Scheduler
components.role: schedules queued packets for transmission on the NIC

components.name: NIC Offloads
components.role: performs scatter/gather, segmentation, and checksum offloads before sending

components.name: Wire
components.role: physical link the packet is finally sent on

content.key_idea: A packet travels through a fixed sequence of buffering and scheduling layers, from application containers down to the wire, each layer a potential source of traffic bursts.
content.reading_order: Strictly left to right, one pipeline stage after another, from App Containers to the Wire.

summary: Figure 2 depicts the conventional Linux network processing pipeline in a containerized deployment, as background for the paper's study of traffic bursts. Application traffic from multiple App Containers passes through TCP/IP socket and transport buffering, then a Container Virtual Switch (bridge) connecting containers to the host stack. Packets (sk_buffs) then reach the Qdiscs, Linux's hierarchical packet schedulers that run in parallel across CPU cores, before being placed in per-queue TX Rings that buffer them ahead of the NIC. Finally, the Network Interface's NIC Scheduler and NIC Offloads stages perform scatter/gather, segmentation, and checksum offloading before the packet is sent on the Wire. The figure is drawn as a simple left-to-right pipeline, with gray funnel icons showing where parallel per-core queues converge or diverge at the Qdiscs and NIC stages.
summary_zh: 图2展示容器化Linux主机中常规网络处理流水线：应用流量经TCP/IP、网桥后到达并行的Qdiscs调度，再进入TX环形缓冲区，最后网卡完成分散/聚合、分段与校验和卸载后发送到链路，作为论文研究流量突发的背景架构。
